newsitem.title: ITALY: Alitalia seeks ally, KLM preferred.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia seeks ally, KLM preferred.

text.p: Italian flag carrier Alitalia is seeking an international alliance by the end of the year, with Dutch airline KLM as the prime contender, the chairman of state industrial holding Iri said in a newspaper interview on Tuesday.

Gian Maria Gros-Pietro, chairman of state holding Iri which controls Alitalia, said in an interview with Il Sole 24-Ore that after starting to address financial problems, the Italian airline was more interesting for investors.
"After having started its restructuring, Alitalia has become more appetizing and it will be able to forge the alliance it seeks by the end of 1997," Gros-Pietro said.
"Of the possible partners KLM and (French carrier) Air France are in pole position," he said.
Gros Pietro said an alliance with KLM was more likely because the airport "hubs" of Milan and Amsterdam were far enough apart for the airlines' businesses not to overlap.
"An alliance with the French might cause too many overlaps. But with KLM, the distance between the hubs...favours the respective needs of each," he said.

Gros Pietro said Iri aimed to privatize Alitalia in two to three years. "If we sold it now, the price would inevitably be very low. To get a good price it is necessary to attract varied shareholders, finish our restructuring plan and find the right partner. We could do it in two years."
The European Commission earlier this month cleared a restructuring plan for Alitalia, approving payment of 2.75 trillion lire ($1.54 million) in state-funded aid to the ailing carrier.
Clearance came with various conditions, including a requirement that the airline sell its holding in the Hungarian carrier Malev.
Transport Minister Claudio Burlando said last week Alitalia made a profit of 10 billion lire for the first half of 1997.
The airline made a group net consolidated loss of 1.203 trillion lire in 1996, its ninth year of losses in a row.
